frozen_claim: Connectome controllability metrics carry target-ranking information beyond degree and strength.

observable.name: incremental_auc_controllability_over_degree_strength
observable.definition: Held-out AUC increment of a model that adds average and modal controllability features to a degree+strength baseline, when ranking nodes for a declared target. On a synthetic modular stochastic-block connectome (n=200, 8 communities, p_in=0.35, p_out=0.01, lognormal weights) with 25 planted connector hubs, the target is the planted hub set (ground truth, not metric-derived). Predictors are standardised and fit with logistic regression under 5-fold x 10-repeat cross-validation; the increment is full-model AUC minus degree+strength AUC, with a bootstrap 95% CI (500 resamples). A degree-preserving null (double-edge-swap rewiring with the empirical weight multiset re-attached) is run for comparison.

model.generative: Modular SBM: 200 nodes in 8 equal communities, within-module edge probability 0.35 and between-module 0.01, lognormal edge weights. 25 randomly chosen nodes are planted as connector hubs by adding cross-module edges, making them bridge modules by construction. Connectivity is enforced via a minimum spanning tree if needed.
model.config: n=200, K=8, planted_hubs=25, estimator=LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000) with StandardScaler, 5-fold x 10-repeat CV AUC, bootstrap=500, null_graphs=40, seed=11.
model.controls: degree-preserving null: the edge topology is rewired by double-edge-swap (preserving the degree sequence) and the empirical weight multiset is re-attached; if controllability captured unique structure the observed increment would exceed the null, which it does not (40th percentile).

thresholds.decision_rule: PRO is accepted only if controllability improves held-out AUC by >= 0.05 over degree+strength AND the bootstrap 95% CI excludes zero AND the degree-preserving null does not reproduce the gain. PRO is rejected if degree/strength matches the full model within +/-0.02 AUC OR controllability is linearly explained by degree+strength with R^2 >= 0.95.

nulls: degree_preserving_rewire: double-edge-swap preserving the degree sequence with the empirical weight multiset re-attached; controllability should not beat degree+strength on rewired graphs if its signal is just degree/strength.
increment measured by repeated cross-validation to limit optimistic bias.
failure_modes: Synthetic substrate only: cannot establish what controllability does on a real empirical connectome (HCP, Glasser-360) with a real behavioural/functional target - the decisive external-validity limitation.
A single graph realization at seed 11; planted-hub target is very easy (hubs have high degree), compressing AUC near the ceiling and limiting headroom for any metric.
Controllability computed for linear time-invariant dynamics; nonlinear or stochastic regimes untested.
Logistic regression with a fixed feature set; a different learner or richer controllability featurization could shift the measured increment.
accepted_evidence_criteria: The thesis is supported on this substrate only if the controllability-augmented model improves held-out AUC by >= 0.05 over degree+strength with a bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero and the degree-preserving null failing to reproduce the gain.
rejected_evidence_criteria: The thesis is rejected on this substrate if degree/strength matches the full model within +/-0.02 AUC, or if controllability is linearly explained by degree+strength with R^2 >= 0.95. This synthetic test cannot establish the REAL-DATA version of the claim even when the thesis fails here; that would require an empirical connectome with a pre-registered directed target.
